facts.fact: The OECD AI Policy Observatory entry, updated 28 April 2026, lists Cameroon's National AI Strategy (SNIA), run by the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications, with status 'Proposed or under development' and start year 2025, while its text says it was unveiled in July 2025.

TechAfrica News reports that the government officially launched its first National AI Strategy (SNIA), unveiled by the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications at the second CONIA consultations; the date is the article's publication date.
L'Economie reports that the national AI development strategy was unveiled by the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications at CONIA on 7-8 July 2025.

facts.fact: ITWeb reports Cameroon is fine-tuning its draft National Strategy for the Development of AI, discussed at national consultations in Yaounde the previous day (7 July 2025).
The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications announced on 21 January 2025 that Cameroon is developing a national AI strategy, which is under development with no adoption stated.

The Nkafu Policy Institute brief states that Cameroon launched its National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (SNIA) in July 2025, with targets to 2040 of 60,000 AI professionals, 12,000 direct AI jobs and 0.8-1.2% of GDP.

note: A proposed AI Council is only recommended by the brief, so no body fact; no funding stated.
Regional CIPESA piece; Cameroon is named only on the Maputo Protocol, and nothing is stated of its AI strategy.
Document only lists recommendations of the CONIA 2024 consultations; states no delivered thing.

facts.fact: A law firm says that, after a public tender, the Government of Cameroon through the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications selected it to lead drafting of the National Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence, with an implementation and financing plan and a government AI roadmap.
facts.system: National Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence

facts.fact: The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications issued a restricted national tender on 17 September 2024 to recruit a firm to draft Cameroon's national AI strategy and government roadmap, estimated at XAF 60 million, with a three-month execution.
Minister Minette Libom Li Likeng said the government is developing an AI development strategy, with national AI consultations held (Business in Cameroon, relaying Cameroon Tribune).

Remy Takang, in a September 2026 policy brief, found that the AI authority, presidential council, regulatory sandboxes and national computing infrastructure envisaged in Cameroon's national AI strategy were not in place.

note: Convening report; states nothing this study asks for this country.

facts.fact: The PATNUC national coordinator says the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications has elaborated an AI strategic development plan that is receiving attention at government level and awaits validation by the competent institutions.

OBS-CC's tracker says Cameroon's National AI Development Strategy (SNIA, seven pillars, horizon 2040) was presented and adopted at the national consultations in Yaounde, and notes no public full text has been found.

The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications unveiled the National AI Strategy (SNIA) on 7 July 2025 at CONIA; Levellers cites OECD.AI listing its status as proposed or under development and says its proposed AI authority and council are not established.

The Guardian Post reports that the 2nd National Consultations on Artificial Intelligence (CONIA 2025, Yaounde, 7-8 July 2025, under MINPOSTEL) ended with stakeholders adopting a national AI strategy, with no cabinet approval or government validation stated.
